text: This is Max Miller speaking from Los Angeles.
The date is September 14, 1957.
And before this microphone, we have Robert C. Gardner of Francisco,
a lecturer of note on the flying saucer MiG-2.
Mr. Gardner, as the first question in this interview,
I wonder if you would care to tell us just what you think flying saucers are.
Well, I think the flying saucers is a catch-all term
to cover all of the unidentified flying object phenomena, or UFO,
recently referred to.
And being a catch-all term,
flying saucers covers a rather complex situation.
That is to say, many people think of flying saucers
in the sense of always thinking of a disc-shaped
or round-shaped aircraft.
However, this is only one of many different types of airfoils
or designs that have been observed in the sky
by rather credible observers.
So I think it's very important to emphasize the fact that flying saucers is a catch-all term
to cover many different types of objects seen flying in our skies
and having been seen by some rather expert and credible observers.
Do you feel qualified to research into these phenomena?
Well, yes, on two or three counts.
One, I am a graduate of an Air Force school.
I was trained in aircraft identification and construction, and I was in the Air Force in the last war.
On the second point, I feel that I was or am somewhat qualified on the basis at least of an intense interest.
I first read Major Kelo's book back in his first book called Flying Saucers Are Real back in the latter part of 1949.
I did make at least one good sighting on my own.
and these things re-stimulated my interest
and I think a genuine enthusiasm and interest
helps a person to be qualified
because if you're sincerely
and intensely interested in a subject
I think you're doing the best that you can
on the level of your training
to search out the facts of the matter.
Yes.
Well, how extensively, might I ask,
have you investigated these subjects?
I have tried to track down
what I consider to be credible reports.
However, it sometimes turns out that these things are mistaken identifications
of one kind or another, but I have traveled throughout the United States and Europe,
interviewed officials, Air Force and airline pilots,
both in the United States and Europe,
have corresponded widely on the subject,
and I feel that it's about as extensive and intensive as just one person
a private investigation could do.
Now, you mentioned that you had sighted a flying saucer yourself several years ago.
Would you care to describe it at all?
We were on a picnic one afternoon south of San Francisco on a place called Skyline Boulevard.
That's you and your wife.
No, there were six of us on a picnic.
There were three couples.
Yes.
And it was about 4.30 in the afternoon.
The sun was at our back.
and there were two of these objects came out of the north, flying in a subtly direction,
and since the sun was at our back and we were looking toward the east,
we were not blinded and we had excellent observation conditions.
The weather was clear, and one of them kept right on going in a south-southeast direction
and was soon out of sight, and the other one hovered, I would say, a matter of a few thousand feet from us at the most.
That is, at the greatest distance, it was not more than a few thousand feet away.
Yes.
And hovered for a few seconds, and then in a tremendous burst of speed,
it was gone out of sight in a few seconds to the south.
That must have been quite interesting.
Yes, it was a rather surprising thing to me,
because one of the girls in the party said,
oh, there go a couple of flying saucers.
And I thought, who's trying to kid who?
And she said, no, look up there.
So I did think that she was serious at that point,
I had my first and I would say probably my only real good sighting.
Yes.
Did they look metallic, physical objects?
They looked physical, but they didn't, well, they weren't necessarily metallic.
They had a definite outline.
Yes.
Rather hard to be certain whether they were metallic or not.
Mm-hmm.
Was there anything in the local newspaper or digital look about this sighting?
Yes.
Yes, and I called the Oakland Airfield and Center, and they said that they'd had a few other reports about that same time.
Oh, really?
Yeah.
So I got more or less a confirmation to that extent.
I wonder if this sighting intensified your interest in the subject of UFOs.
Well, yes, it certainly re-stimulated it, although I had been interested.
You see, that was in August of 1952, that is my sighting, and I had been interested since 1949.
Yes.
but it certainly has stimulated more activity, I can imagine.
In your research, you must have studied some of the Air Force reports on these phenomena.
Now, I wonder if you can tell us if you believe the Air Force is hiding facts from the public,
if their reports are contradictory to you, as so many other researchers and authors seem to feel,
and if so, you might indicate why you think these reports are so contradictory.
place definitely do believe that they are hiding at least some of the facts. I think
part of the contradictory reports are due to the fact that the PIO officer, that is
the public information officer, that any definite or particular area have not checked out their
release with the Pentagon in Washington, and therefore the Pentagon will issue a statement
later on. Upon further investigation and study, et cetera, et cetera, we find that such and
usually play down the thing quite considerably.
Yes, I see.
Do you know if there are any definite orders instigated by the Air Force
to prohibit the Air Force pilots, airline pilots in general,
or military personnel from revealing any findings they may make to the press or public?
Well, yes.
Aren't there some official statements on that?
You probably could give them a more verbatim word as to what those restrictions are.
I know there are such.
Well, particularly thinking of AFR or Air Force Regulation 200-2,
I would take it that your opinion might be in accordance with mine.
This regulation is probably an extreme and definitely has been instigated to withhold certain facts.
I think it should be rescinded.
Might I ask if you concur likewise?
Yes, I certainly feel that naturally being eager to get more information should be reserved.
if you might care to opine as to just why the government is keeping these data secret?
Oh, I think there is a combination of reasons.
For instance, I was in the Pentagon in Washington,
and I was interviewed, if you want to call it that,
by several officers there in Air Force Intelligence.
I was impressed by the fact that even though they were all wearing the same uniform,
they did not all think alike.
Definitely that some thought that the information should be more generally released.
However, they were under orders as to what to say.
A general approach, namely, that the flying saucers did not exist.
They spent several hours trying to convince me that flying saucers didn't exist.
Did they?
They did that.
And my reaction was, gentlemen, there is too much protestation here.
If they don't exist, so what?
They don't exist.
But why go to all this trouble if that has convinced me they don't exist?
An excellent point.
thing was that at the end of this several hours of trying to convince me of this, one
of the officers spoke up and said, well, Mr. Gardner, one of the reasons we have an Air
Force is to defend freedom of speech.
Amen to that. And while you were at the Pentagon, I wonder if you attempted to see any of the
Air Force's official files of their investigation of UFO phenomena.
Yes, I did attempt to do that, but Chop was the famous PIO man at the time.
Is this Albert M. Chop?
Yeah, that's right.
And a funny thing I had known about Al Chop and been a casual friend of his for many years before he was in this official position.
Yes.
In fact, his closest friend lived in our house for a number of years.
Is that right?
which gave me sort of an inside track there.
And I said, come on, Al, don't kid me after all.
I mean, we're friends here.
But, of course, he had an official job to perform there,
namely to deny the existence of these things.
And so anything that I was given at that time,
I was quite impressed with the fact that it was nothing new.
And I was also impressed with the fact that they had a lot of information.
And Mr. Chopp may have been very innocent at the time.
that this other information existed.
Therefore, he was being sincere and convincing
because he didn't know any different.
Yes.
Well, I think that Al Kopp is more recently,
at least subsequent to his retirement from the Air Force,
that he has stated that flying saucers
are in all probability interplanetary,
more or less confirming your own thesis along this line,
to a certain degree, anyway.
I wonder if you can tell me if you believe the Air Force
or whether or not you believe the Air Force
its files and findings on these phenomena.
Well, now, I have stuck my neck out a little bit in the past.
The first magazine article I wrote on the subject, which appeared in 1953,
I stated that I thought that the Air Force would, from the information I had at that time.
But being subsequently disappointed in more than one occasion,
I am now of the opinion that since they kept the atomic bomb a secret
until they were very much ready to release the information.
I think the same thing will be done with the saucer situation,
and I think it will be quite some time.
I really believe that they will not release anything
until they're forced to by something that possibly occurs,
because I think that as far as interplanetary saucers go,
there are many things that they do not know about the situation themselves.
For an example, those in the higher echelons who are in the know,
about a certain UFO report where jets are vectored to pursue.
Yes.
Now, the men in the know, of course, realize the possibility
that there are many things that we don't know about these things,
and it could be, at least in some cases, rather dangerous.
And it could, as General Chiblaw told me in a long interview at Air Force Base
when he was Continental Defense Commander,
he said that we have lost many officers, pilots, and planes,
to intercept the UFO.
That's amazing.
That's quite a statement,
and I did not reveal this publicly
until after his retirement.
Yes.
Even at the time,
he did not say that I couldn't repeat it,
but I respected his position
until after he did retire.
Would you care to tell me approximately
when this interview took place?
Yes.
It took place in March of 1953.
Yes, well, that's unusually interesting.
Was that Met Air Force Base?
Air Force Base ENT at Colorado Springs.
I see.
And to progress the more controversial facet of this research,
I wonder if you would care to tell us what you think of the many little men stories,
the crashed saucer stories, especially those prevalent around Europe and South America in 1953,
or rather in 1954 and 55, also those expounded by Frank Scully in his book,
Behind the Flying Saucers.
Well, to answer the last part of the question,
in the first place as a swell fellow,
and did the very best that he could at the time in which he wrote his book,
Behind the Flying Saucers.
You know, J.P. Kahn, a reporter of the San Francisco Chronicle,
told me in a private interview that here Frank Scully wrote the book called
Behind the Flying Saucers.
He was going to try to write an expose and call it Behind Frank Scully.
Now, I think that a character assassination attempt was made there.
I don't think it was completely successful at all.
He certainly did not assassinate a lot of the facts.
Frank Scully had a man there.
I think it was a question of possibly getting a little misinformation mixed up with some real good information.
I see.
And then they tried to discredit the whole thing.
Yes.
Well, along this general line of landings and little men and whatnot,
what do you think of these many contact stories that have arisen in the past, oh, three or four years?
Well, I think that possibly they seem to be so persistent and the people seem to be so sincere.
I am forced to believe that some of them must have some basis in truth.
Yes.
As just to which ones and how extensive or how much these stories were elaborated on.
You know how it is.
When we have an experience, we might get a little overenthusiastic.
And as the story goes on, it gets better and better.
as to what actually originally happened, I don't know.
I do feel that there have been some genuine contacts, however.
Well, that's the most objective comment, I feel,
and switching to a more objective side of flying sausage as well.
Are your opinions generally in accord with those of Major Donald E. Kehoe
as expressed in all his many talks and in his last three books on the flying saucer topic?

Well, I will say this. As far as he goes, I would say that my opinions are very much in accord with Donald Kehoe. I talked with him several times when I was in Washington. He lives in Arlington, Virginia, and we met together a few times and had some chats, and I think he's done an excellent job.
I think his books are as well documented as any that I know,
and certainly would be a credible addition to any library on the subject.
Yes, I see.
Would you recommend them fairly highly, then?
I would say so.
Major Kehoe, of course, believes that flying saucers have an origin outside of this planet,
that is, extraterrestrially.
There is a research chemist in White Plains, New York,
who has gone into this phenomenon, he says, for several years,
and he's come to the conclusion that they are manufactured right here on Earth,
that is, by the United States or Russia.
I think he says the United States.
Now, do you concur with this latter theory?
Yes, I firmly believe this,
and I think if given enough time and an impartial group of people, I could actually prove it.
In fact, I have a serial number of one of our craft that crashed in Trinity Bay near Baytown, Texas.

Yes. I have the information that was taken off of that flying saucer. Besides that, I have other information, which I think is overwhelming. At that particular time, we had our saucer aircraft, among others. There were two that were referred to as the Lark and the Loon.
Oh.
And then, of course, at the end of the war, the Russians, unfortunately,
I say unfortunately because I think we should have taken over the German rocket base at Pinnemünde,
nevertheless, they not only took over the rockets there,
but they also took over a circular disc-shaped aircraft
which the Germans had almost gotten into the air,
which they designated as Model Number A-4.
This craft was rather remarkable.
It would fly a minimum of 1,500 miles an hour
could rise vertically into the air.
Yes.
The Russians took off from that point and developed their own flying saucer.
I see.
So I think the mass sightings that have been made by the Swedish and Norwegian airline and Air Force pilots
from Russian-occupied territory and Russian territory itself are largely of Russian origin.
But you feel, then, that both major world powers, the United States and Russia, have developed these types of aircraft?
And the British, too.
And the British, yes.

Both the United States Air Force and Navy Air Force, the British Air Force and the Russian Air Force all have rather relatively advanced disc-shaped flying aircraft, both piloted and remotely controlled.
Virtually all researchers into these phenomena believe that reports of flying saucers, or UFOs, have been reported from all countries of this planet, at least all three countries.
With this in mind, do you believe that any world power would be willing to exhibit a
fallible, and of course anything Earth made would be fallible, such a fallible secret
weapon, such a top secret device before alien eyes?
Because there is always the possibility that such a device could be either captured or
it could on its own crash be destroyed or in some fashion or other divulge the secret,
or at least the mode of operation or mode of propulsion, as the case may be.
I think they would be willing to gamble that, yes.
I do feel that they would be willing to gamble it because the stakes are pretty high.
And as a matter of fact, perhaps you have heard of that one that was supposed to have crashed,
the Russian saucer that was supposed to have crashed north of Spitsbergen in Norway,
and they claim that they found the Russian symbols on the control panels.
Yes, as a matter of fact, I have.
Although the last data I read on that was in Bob Gribble's APRG Reporter, and this was, oh, I think four or five months ago.
And he quoted an article, and I believe it was from a Norwegian newspaper.
Of course, it would naturally be about the most authoritative.
However, I have tried to have the data confirmed, and this has not been done.
It is difficult to say why.
This report may have been a hoax, or it may not have been.
This story or incident in this newspaper indicated, perhaps it was the magazine,
that the saucer or UFO did crash and was found and was examined by Norwegian and other countries' Air Force officers.
However, it contradicted the earlier statement that Russian symbols, etc., had been found,
and it gave every connotation that this object or artifact was non-terrestrial,
or perhaps some symbols, et cetera, found in it or on it were undecipherable
or perhaps some metallic substance could not be analyzed
or was found to be unavailable on this planet.
I don't remember right now.
However, I don't think this could be validly used to argue the case in either way
because it is unconfirmed, as I said previously.
Sometimes these things are a little bit difficult to be positively certain of.
We can only say that there are indications along that line.
Yes.
I would take it, then, that you do not believe that flying saucers are interplanetary.
Is this correct?
Oh, that's not correct.
No, this is not correct, Max.
The situation is that I feel we have two major sources, terrestrial and extraterrestrial.
Oh.
Then both of those sources break down into two subcategories.
Yes.
The terrestrial origins, one, are the ones that I mentioned,
the United States Air Force, Navy Air Force, British Air Force, and Russian Air Force,
and then certain flying objects from very little known and remote hidden areas,
land areas where the white man has seldom set foot.
Yes.
This is a little-mentioned source, but I think a very important source of this phenomena.
Then the extraterrestrial phenomena break down into two major categories,
namely the very solid third-dimensional origin,
and then the more nebulous or fourth-dimensional,
or what the Air Force chooses to call the out-of-phase aspects of physical reality.
I see.
But you would, I would take it then, from what you've said,
that you believe that the sighting reports coming from various parts of the world
have predominantly stemmed from these terrestrially created aircraft.
I think that, put it this way,
that a major portion of the disc-shaped aircraft scene
has been of a very earthly origin.
Yes.
But then there seems to be a certain line that we can draw
and say, well, beyond that,
certain types of aircraft definitely have the flavor of the interplanetary class.
I see.
Rolling along here with reference to the non-terrestrial objects or flying saucers or UFOs,
do you believe that these particular crafts have a hostile or friendly intent to their motive?
Well, now, in most all the cases that I've ever been able to check down thoroughly,
by first checking the reputation of the people making the reports
and then investigating the reports and analyzing what they have reported,
I feel that in most all of these cases, the UFO, that is the unidentified flying object or flying saucer,
has tried, has attempted to take an evasive action and get away from any conflict or attack
or anything that would be classified as offensive.
I think this is almost invariably true.
So generally speaking, I could say that they certainly show a friendly intent.
intent. But, besides that point, there have been cases of where our craft have been, well,
I feel maybe we could go as strong as to say they're actually shot down or disabled.
Oh, really?
Where they've had to defend themselves in order to get away or something.
Yes. Would you care to give an opinion as to where these objects may originate from,
that is, any particular planet or outside of this solar system?
Well, since we have such, as I had mentioned in the earlier part of our discussion here,
that we have such a variety of shapes and sizes,
I think it's logical to assume,
even though we have a variety of shapes and sizes of our own aircraft on the planet Earth,
I do think that the variety in shapes and sizes
and the fact that these things have been seen for many, many decades
indicate that they could be coming both from our solar system
and from outside our solar system.
Yes, from, say, both Mars and a distant star system.
That's right.
I feel that that's distinctly possible.
Mm-hmm.
Well, I noticed that you said that these reports, as we all know,
have come in a variety of shapes and sizes and colors and everything else.
Disregarding that fact for a minute,
do you believe that there are any segments of sightings, say,
or along that line that could be classified into any pattern or patterns
or colors, sizes, shapes, etc., outside of the general cigar or disc-shaped craft?
I think, as I had mentioned earlier in the discussion, too,
I said that these take such a wide variety that I think it would be difficult to say
that there were a pattern of any shapes and sizes or colors.
It seems to be so varied.
As Major General James Sanford, Chief of Air Force Intelligence, has put it,
he said that there has been no pattern, as he worded it, I think,
No pattern of any threat.
Oh, that's for the United States.
No pattern of any threat.
Yes, underlined.
I wonder if you would care to relate any particularly dramatic or conclusive UFO sightings that you have found in your researches.
Oh, I think it would be difficult to limit that to any one case.
I think there have been some rather dramatic and certainly exciting and unusual reports.

For an example, to give you an idea of a little drama and action at the same time, not too long ago there were a flight of six Navy jet fighters over the general Hawaiian Island archipelago, that is the Hawaiian Island area, in a routine training flight there.
The report comes from a Navy commander, I'll not mention his name, who knew some of the boys that were involved in this.
He said that six flying saucers, perhaps maybe coincidentally, perhaps not coincidentally, perhaps more significantly,
six flying saucers came down out of the sky from a higher elevation,
and each one of the saucers picked out an individual Navy jet fighter
and they flew right on their wingtips for quite a little distance.
And after a short distance, they apparently deliberately tilted over sideways in their flying
so that their top, this bubble or dome-shaped top,
was very easily visible, say, at a distance of not more than 30 feet,
which is extremely close, of course.
And the boys were able to land their planes after this experience,
and that's just about all because they said that the occupants of these craft
were so frightening that they were almost beyond description.
Now, I still say that it's possible that these were space suits
or pressurized suits of some kind which gave this grotesque appearance
because, you know, our own space and high-altitude flying suits
are rather grotesque in appearance,
They may not have seen the real occupants of the saucers.
They may have only seen what was covering them up.
Well, that's a dramatic UFO report, all right.
And digressing here, I note that in a recent Trendex national survey,
it indicated that approximately 25.3% of the public, at least those queried,
indicated their belief that UFOs could, and could, of course, is emphasized here,
that UFOs could originate from outside of this planet.
Was this Tremex report made?
It was made, let me see, as of this recording,
it was made about three weeks ago,
or sometime around the mid or late of August.
In several cities, was it?
It was released out of New York.
Yes, it was made.
It was a national survey.
How expensive it was, I don't know.
It was published in the Indianapolis Star.
I think about, let's see,
about 25% of the public said that they didn't know or didn't opine as to whether or not they thought flying saucers were real or not,
and about 51 or so percent indicated they thought UFOs were either non-existent,
hallucinations, misidentifications of weather balloons,
or some type of craft made right here on our planet, as you have earlier indicated.
But I was wondering, from your lecture series around the country, particularly here on the West Coast,
interest in flying saucers has been increasing or decreasing over the past, oh, five years, say.
Well, it's a strange thing.
I frankly think that the press services have not picked up reports as much as they used to
because I think they consider it old hat in many cases.
On the other hand, I think as far as the public goes,
there is greater interest today than there ever has been before.
and not only that, I think there are as many or more sightings today than ever before.
I think they're just generally receiving less attention probably.
Well, I imagine that's rather true,
particularly in regard with this earlier mentioned Trendex report.
Now, going along here,
do you believe that there are many frogs and or crap pots in this field of research?
Well, now that's an interesting question. I feel that most all of the people are sincere.
I do feel that some people let their imagination and their enthusiasm carry them into a realm
where to other people they might seem a crackpot. If they had a little more control of their
Their enthusiasm, perhaps, and their sincerity might not give this appearance.
But from an impartial standpoint, I suppose that you could say that there were certainly these type of individuals.
However, I think even those individuals in most cases are sincere, but they're just a little carried away.
I wonder if you have interviewed any other noted personages or authorities in this or other fields besides General Benjamin Chidlon Major Donald Kehoe.
Well, I was a guest of Arthur Clark, the president of the British Interplanetary Society in his home in London.
Oh, really?
We had a long way into the night discussion.
And you may know that within the last few weeks, his latest book has been out.
And it's quite interesting.
interesting. He has been rather objective in this whole subject. And of course, he's
quite a prominent person, has written many books on the subject. He's a recognized physicist.
Yes.
He would certainly be classified as an interesting personality that I've had a long
talk with about the matter. Oh, there have been many national newscasters who have interviewed
You'd be on their news programs, and we've talked privately both before and after the broadcast.

of course, having been in the Air Force myself, having lived on top of Air Technical Intelligence Command at Dayton, Ohio, for 25 years,
I sometimes had, you might say, a pipeline in there, which was a rather fortunate connection, to say the least,
That and other authors of various books and other lecturers, of course, have been, take for example, Gerald Hurd.
Oh, yes.
He wrote the book Another World Watching and then subsequently had another sequel out to that,
which was expanded a little more, added two to bring it up to date.
Yes.
General, along those lines, various people.
Well, I believe that you've probably made more radio and TV appearances and interviews, et cetera,
fine thoughts or
personalities that I know of.
Have you any idea just how many of these appearances
you have made? Well, Max, I
tried to
keep track of it, and when it got over a hundred,

hookups several times,
both on radio and television,
and as you know,

days, so that's

mixed in between lectures
and showing my motion picture

it keeps you hustling.

back to the contact stories,
you indicated at least
partial and qualified belief
in some of these accounts.
I was wondering if you feel
that we may eventually effect
a worldwide or universal contact,
in other words,
a meeting of the world?
I believe that this will come about.
It's always hard when you go ahead in time, it's always hard to say when.
Nobody can say when, really.
There have been a lot of prophecies and forecasts and so forth,
some accurate and some not so accurate.
But I do believe that eventually we can look forward to more contact,
which will be much more in the open than presently we have.
Yes. Do you feel this will be affected gradually?
I think it will be affected gradually.
However, I think when it begins generally that it will accelerate more or less rapidly.
In other words, it may be gradual for a period of years now,
but I think definitely in our time there will be a point reached
where this thing will accelerate considerably in its importance and in actual contact.
Would you care to hazard a guess as to just why these UFOs are visiting this planet at this time?
Well, I think we covered the ground earlier in this discussion,
since they could be from both the solar system and outside of the solar system.
As far as them being here is concerned, I think it's pertinent to interplanetary varieties.
Yes.
I think they are looking us over from the standpoint of many interesting observations.
quite apparent, of course, that we have detonated many hydrogen and atomic explosions, and we
have toyed with cobalt and so forth, and we're getting into more unstable elements.
Yes.
I feel it's quite possible that many of these planetary observers have gone through this
stage of development many, many eons ago, or at least quite some time ago, and they're
interested to see how we are handling the situation as we come on it.
Yes.
And then no doubt interested to see what we are doing with other things in our advance of so-called civilization.
I think this is probably a prime point of the reason of them being here.
Other lesser reasons possibly could be to give us help to neutralize radiation fallout,
if they could do so, to be of service in one way or another
without directly interfering with the affairs of the planet.
the mode of propulsion of these spacecraft?
Well, now, that's quite an interesting question.
It involves, to do it justice, quite some discussion.
But if you try to capsulate this and bring it down and condense it,
I think we can compare what we might assume would be interplanetary propulsion
with what we've done ourselves.
Yes.
I personally feel and believe that we have gone through a stage of propeller-driven,
round or disc-shaped aircraft or flying saucers, through jet, through rocket, through atomic,
and we are presently flying our latest aircraft on what I think will become to be known as
electrogravitic drive, which many commonly refer to now as anti-grav or anti-gravity devices.
Yes, I see.
Therefore, I think we can compare and say that foreign sources, as is interplanetary
sources can be possibly utilizing one or a combination of these methods and possibly
using methods of which we are totally ignorant of.
For instance, we had on Earth electricity in clear passage time, but nobody knew it.
Yes.
We also have anti-gravity devices now, which we've been struggling to master for years.
And we've also had that with us for centuries, but we didn't know it.
Yes.
So I think, likewise, there may be elements of electricity, of which we know nothing about now,
and of gravitational interplanetary lines of force, of which we know nothing about,
and realms of the fourth dimension, since our five senses are strictly limited,
which, since we have cutoffs in our hearing perception at about 15,000 cycles,
